To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a novel deep learning based MRI reconstruction method that can be trained in a completely unsupervised fashion, allowing for a single network model that can be applied to different MRI acquisition schemes.
we propose a GAN based reconstruction approach that can be used for arbitrary sampling modalities and that is able to refine the reconstruction quality by adapting the generating network.

the combination of a GAN and an inverse problem solver can be used to reconstruct MRI data from undersampled k space measurements and that the performance of this method can be improved by adapting the GAN to the measured data using the solution of the inverse problem.

our method is able to reconstruct MRI data at high acceleration factors, but it is currently outperformed by state of the art deep learning based techniques that use a supervised training scheme.
the presented approach is an interesting alternative to the state of the art methods for the reconstruction of accelerated MRI data.

our method can be applied to multiple sampling modalities, but it requires an adaption step to the specific problem at hand.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose an iterative reconstruction scheme for accelerated MRI that is able to learn a generic prior distribution of uncorrupt images.
the proposed method allows for the application of a GAN prior to a variety of MRI reconstruction tasks, even if the training data does not match the sampling pattern of the respective task.

the proposed method allows for an unsupervised learning of a generative adversial network that is capable of generating high resolution images of unseen data and that this prior can then be used to accelerate MRI reconstructions without any additional adaption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GANs are able to learn a prior that is useful for MRI reconstruction, and that the refinement scheme is a powerful tool to adapt the GAN prior to the measurement process.
a GAN trained on uncorrupted images is able to provide a useful implicit prior for accelerated MRI reconstruction, which can further be refined by a simple data driven scheme.
a GAN prior can be incorporated into a reconstruction framework in an efficient way, allowing for a flexible and fast implementation.
